question: The line graph shows the unemployment rates in three countries (the UK, the rest of Europe and Japan) between 1993 and 2007. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay:
The line graph compares unemployment rates in the United Kingdom, Japan and the rest of Europe from 1993 to 2007.
  Overall, the proportion of unemployed people declined considerably in the UK, whereas Japan experienced a general increase despite a fall towards the end. In the rest of Europe, the figure initially rose before decreasing. Overall, unemployment fell markedly in the UK, whereas Japan experienced a general increase despite a later decline. The rest of Europe recorded the highest rate for most of the period, while Japan generally had the lowest.

  In 1993, unemployment stood at approximately 11% in the UK, compared with 9% in the rest of Europe. The British figure subsequently fell almost continuously, reaching around 6% in 1999 and bottoming out at just over 4% in 2004. It then recovered modestly to roughly 5.3% by 2007. By contrast, the rate across the rest of Europe climbed to a peak of about 10.5% in 1997. Thereafter, it dropped to 8% in 2001, remained stable until 2005, and finished at approximately 6.5%.
  Japan began with by far the lowest level, at only 2%. Its unemployment rate rose gradually to 3% in 1997 and remained relatively unchanged until 1999. A sharper increase followed, with the figure peaking at 5% in 2002 and 2003 before falling steadily to just above 3% in 2007.

question: The line graph below shows the percentage of the Australian workforce in five industries between 1962 and 2012. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay:
The line chart compares the proportion of the workforce in Australia distributed across five different industries, namely Services, Manufacturing, Agriculture, Construction, and Mining, from 1962 to 2012.
Overall, services were the sector with the largest share of the workforce over the period, with its share increasing considerably, while manufacturing and agriculture experienced the opposite trajectory. In addition, the share of construction remained relatively stable, whereas that of mining showed minor fluctuations.

In 1962, there were just over 50% of Australian employees working in the services industry, roughly twice the figure for manufacturing, at around 27%.  Agriculture and construction employed much smaller proportions, at around 10% and 9%, respectively, whereas mining represented only about 1% of the workforce. Over the following three decades, the share of service-sector employment rose significantly to nearly 72% in 1962, while the manufacturing figure fell to 15%.
These contrasting trends continued over the remaining twenty years. By 2012, services employed just under 80% of Australian workers, widening the gap with manufacturing, whose share had dropped to 10%. Agriculture also declined throughout the period, finishing at approximately 3%, less than a third of its initial level. In addition, construction remained close to 10%, equalling manufacturing by the final year. Mining consistently had the smallest share, fluctuating slightly but remaining below 3%.

question: The graph below shows different sources of air pollutants in the UK from 1990 to 2005. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay:
The line chart compares the amount of air pollution produced by industry, transport, and households in the UK between 1990 and 2005, together with the total amount of pollutants. Units are measured in million tonnes.

Overall, the total level of air pollution fell considerably during the period. Industry was the largest source of pollution, although its figure declined sharply, while transport remained relatively stable. Household emissions also decreased and became almost negligible by 2005.

In 1990, total air pollutants stood at 7 million tonnes. This figure decreased steadily to 5 million tonnes in 1996 and then dropped further to around 3 million tonnes by 2005. A similar trend can be seen in the industry, whose emissions declined from 5.7 million tonnes in 1990 to 3 million tonnes in 1996. By the end of the period. its figure had fallen to nearly 2 million tonnes.

Conversely, transport and households generated much smaller amounts of pollution. Transport emissions stayed close to 1 million tonnes throughout the period, despite some minor fluctuations. Household pollution, meanwhile, declined from nearly 1 million tonnes in 1990 to around 0.4 million tonnes in 1996. Although it rose slightly to 0.5 million tonnes in 1999, it subsequently fell to almost zero in 2005.

question: The line graph illustrates the proportion of mobile phone sales by three manufacturers between 1994 and 2004.
essay:
The line graph compares the market share, as a percentage of sales, for three mobile phone manufacturers( Motorola, Nokia, and Sony Ericsson ) over the decade between 1994 and 2004.

Overall, the period witnessed a dramatic shift in market dominance. Nokia experienced a sharp increase in sales, becoming the industry leader, while Motorola saw a significant decrease, losing its initial top position. Sony Ericsson's market share remained the lowest of the three, showing a slight overall decline.

In 1994, Motorola was the market leader, accounting for approximately 32% of sales. Nokia held the second position with around 21% of the market, and Sony Ericsson was the smallest manufacture, with a share of nearly 11%.

Over the following ten years, Nokia's trajectory changed dramatically. After a brief dip around 1997, its share rose sharply, overtaking Motorola in 1998 and soaring to a peak of roughly 37% in 2002, before finishing at 30%. Conversely, Motorola's figure fell from 32% to a low point of about 14% in 2000, followed by a slight recovery to end at 18%. Sony Ericsson fluctuated between 10-15% until 1998, then entered a general decline to a low of 7%,  in 2003, finally ending the period at approximately 10%.
